items.passage: What great race has ever been won by any man, or by any nation, without some such fall during its course? Have we not all declared that some check to that career was necessary? Men in their pursuit of intelligence had forgotten to be honest; in struggling for greatness they had discarded purity. The nation has been great, but the statesmen of the nation have been little. Men have hardly been ambitious to govern, but they have coveted the wages of governors. Corruption has crept into high places,--into places that should have been high,--till of all holes and corners in the land they have become the lowest. No public man has been trusted for ordinary honesty.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From bitter resentment of a rival nation to cautious praise of its leaders
From playful mockery of statesmen to sincere sympathy for their burdens
From hopeful anticipation of reform to quiet resignation about failure
From reflective acceptance of a setback to blunt condemnation of corruption
items.explanation: 지문 앞부분은 수사 의문문으로 어떤 경주에도 넘어짐은 있으며 그 제동이 필요했다고 차분히 받아들인다. 이후 정치가들이 작았고 부패가 높은 자리에 스며들었다는 문장에서 어조가 날카로운 비판으로 바뀐다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 경쟁 국가, B의 조롱과 동정, C의 개혁에 대한 기대는 지문에 나타나지 않는다.

items.passage:
Upon mentioning this I found that it had been noticed in elm avenues and groups a hundred miles distant, so that it is not a local circumstance.

As far as yet appears, the elms do not seem materially injured, the damage being outwardly confined to the bough attacked. These brown spots looked very remarkable just after the trees had become green. They were quite distinct from the damage caused by the snow of October 1880. The boughs broken by the snow had leaves upon them which at once turned brown, and in the case of the oak were visible, the following spring, as brown spots among the green.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It notes that a tree condition is widespread, assesses its effects, and separates it from earlier damage.
It explains the cause of a tree disease, then proposes a method for preventing its spread.
It recalls a snowstorm in detail, then argues that the storm permanently weakened the elms.
It compares elms and oaks in general, then concludes that oaks are the hardier trees.
items.explanation: 화자는 먼저 갈색 반점이 백 마일 떨어진 곳에서도 관찰되어 지역적 현상이 아니라고 밝힌다. 이어 느릅나무가 크게 손상되지 않았다고 평가하고, 1880년 10월 눈 피해와는 뚜렷이 다르다고 구분한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 원인·예방책, C의 영구적 약화 주장, D의 수종 비교는 지문에 없다.

items.passage: Really, Sir Hugo was worthy of it on his own individual merits. He was a fine young fellow. The foundation of his principles had been laid by a good mother--a widow who had never ceased to mourn for the husband of her youth, whose son, her only child, was the apple of her eye. From her he had derived a remarkable amount of ingenuousness and a dash of enthusiasm, which such intercourse with the world as he had commanded had failed to extinguish. He was regarded as something of a young Quixote at his University, which had been his world for the most part, but he had possessed wit to defend his views. He was manly, rather rash, and a little thoughtless; but in his very thoughtlessness he was generous and honest--a lad to be liked first and trusted afterwards.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a mother's grief, then shows how her sorrow eventually ruined her son.
It asserts a young man's merit, traces the source of his principles, and summarizes his traits.
It recounts a university quarrel, then explains how a young man was punished for it.
It lists a young man's faults, then reveals that others refused to trust him.
items.explanation: 지문은 먼저 휴고 경이 자신의 장점만으로도 그럴 자격이 있다고 단언한다. 이어 그의 원칙의 토대가 어머니에게서 왔다고 설명하고, 마지막에 성급함과 관대함 같은 성격을 요약한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 몰락, C의 처벌, D의 불신은 지문 내용과 어긋난다.

items.passage:
We cannot suppose that life would develop in any important degree in a region of perpetual frost, such as the polar regions of our globe. But we do not find any end to it as the climate becomes warmer. On the contrary, every one knows that the tropics are the most fertile regions of the globe in its production. The luxuriance of the vegetation and the number of the animals continually increase the more tropical the climate becomes. Where the limit may be set no one can say. But it would doubtless be far above the present temperature of the equatorial regions.

It has often been said that this does not apply to the human race, that men lack vigor in the tropics.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes polar wildlife, then argues that cold regions support the most life.
It questions whether tropical regions exist, then defends that claim with examples.
It presents a claim linking warmth to abundant life, then introduces an objection about humans.
It praises human vigor in the tropics, then explains why vegetation is scarce there.
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 영구 동토에서는 생명이 발달하기 어렵지만 기후가 따뜻할수록 동식물이 늘어난다고 주장한다. 그 뒤 새 문단에서 이 원리가 인류에는 적용되지 않는다는, 열대에서 사람이 활력을 잃는다는 반론을 소개한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A, B, D는 지문의 주장과 반대이거나 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
Stepping back before that extraordinary salutation, Judge Whaley saw a man come forward leading a woman by the hand. __The Judge receded until he could go no farther, and sank into his chair.__ The woman knelt at his feet; older, and grown gray and in the robes of humility, yet in countenance as she had been, only purified, as it seemed, by suffering and repentance, he saw his wife of more than twenty years before.

Looking up into the face of the son he had watched so long for, the old man saw a still more wonderful transformation. The elegant young gentleman of a few months before was a living spectre, his bright eyes standing out large and consumptive upon a transparent skin, and glittering with fanaticism or excitement.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reveals that the Judge has long been ill and can no longer stand unaided.
It suggests that the Judge is angry and plans to order the visitors away.
It indicates that the Judge has failed to recognize anyone in the room.
It conveys the Judge's overwhelming shock as the visitors approach him.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장에서 판사는 더 물러설 수 없을 때까지 뒷걸음질하다가 의자에 주저앉는다. 바로 앞의 놀라운 인사와 뒤이어 드러나는 아내와 아들의 변한 모습은 그가 큰 충격을 받았음을 보여 준다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 지병, B의 분노, C의 알아보지 못함은 지문 근거가 없다.

items.passage: I shook my head and passed on. Notwithstanding the distance that lay between us, I could plainly see the look of astonishment that overspread her beautiful face. She had started to meet me, almost in a run, but when she perceived that I was avoiding her she came to a sudden halt, and the little basket she held in her hand instantly fell to the ground, scattering the flowers round her feet, while she appeared to be struck dumb with wonder. __What could I do?__ Had I not given my most solemn promise not to speak to her until Mr. Rockland could have an interview with her? When I saw the painful expression of her dear face I wheeled round and started toward her; then recollecting the promise I had made, I hastened away.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces the narrator's sense of being torn between his feelings and his promise.
It shows that the narrator has forgotten why he is avoiding the young woman.
It suggests that the narrator is annoyed by the young woman's dropped flowers.
It reveals that the narrator plans to ask Mr. Rockland to release him.
items.explanation: 화자는 여인의 놀란 얼굴을 보고도 지나치다가 밑줄 문장으로 어찌할 수 없는 처지를 드러낸다. 바로 다음 문장에서 그는 엄숙한 약속을 떠올리고, 마지막에는 돌아섰다가 다시 서둘러 떠난다. 따라서 밑줄 문장은 감정과 약속 사이의 갈등을 제시하므로 A가 정답이다. B, C, D는 지문 내용과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Of course there are the illiterates and the almost illiterate. But, numerous though they are, they do not count for much in this republic. They do not decide elections. They do not select candidates. They do not propose and compel legislation. The so-called ignorant vote is not a national or a local peril. It is not a national, rarely even a local factor.

__The ignorance that counts in a Democracy is educated ignorance.__ Sometimes it has only been part of the way through the common schools. Sometimes it has one or more university degrees. Sometimes it struts and preens itself as “the scholar in politics.” Only too often it writes books, especially histories, and in the magazines and in the newspapers tells how and for whom we ought to vote.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It concedes that illiterate voters are the main danger to the republic.
It shifts the focus from a group dismissed as unimportant to the group the author finds influential.
It summarizes a scholar's argument that the author later accepts without question.
It proposes that universities should stop awarding degrees to politicians.
items.explanation: 첫 문단에서 글쓴이는 문맹자들이 선거나 입법을 좌우하지 않으므로 위험이 아니라고 말한다. 밑줄 문장은 진짜 문제가 되는 것은 교육받은 무지라고 하며 초점을 옮기고, 이후 문장들이 그 집단을 묘사한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 글쓴이의 주장과 반대이고 C, D는 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Up to the present time no stigma has been attached to my irregularities, none have suspected that I was less than I claimed to be--a soldier and a gentleman, betrothed to the noblest woman in the world. But this manner of living in the end works the destruction of habits and reputation to any who continue in it. To be brief, I have found political life nothing but a commerce. All have their price, and the highest sometimes sell out the cheapest. Men are estimated here by their boldness and breadth only, and a single successful venture of the kind I have in hand will dismiss me from this city rich and without exposure, and I swear never again to be seen in the lobbies of the Federal legislature.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward political life?
options: He admires it as a noble calling that rewards honest service.
He fears it because his secret has already been exposed in public.
He is indifferent to it, since he plans to stay in the city forever.
He views it with cynical contempt, seeing it as a trade in which anyone can be bought.
items.explanation: 화자는 정치 생활이 결국 상거래에 지나지 않으며 모두에게 값이 있다고 말한다. 또 한 번의 성공한 거래로 부자가 되어 떠난 뒤 다시는 의회 로비에 나타나지 않겠다고 맹세한다. 따라서 냉소적 경멸을 나타낸 D가 정답이다. A는 반대이고, 아직 의심받지 않았다고 했으므로 B, 떠나겠다고 했으므로 C도 틀리다.

items.passage: When I arrived at home I of course went to see Lottie before talking with any one else. I found my darling all that heart could wish. She was more beautiful, more charming in my eyes than ever. The large, dreamy blue eyes were swimming in tears of joy as I held her to my glad heart, and I saw a look of love that satisfied me that I was the possessor of a treasure of great value. I lingered by my darling’s side until late at night. Every little trifling incident was described--the days of old were alluded to and discussed, while the present and future came in for a full share.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Lottie?
options: Deep affection and delight in her company
Polite respect mixed with quiet doubt
Mild irritation at her emotional display
Guilty unease about his long absence
items.explanation: 화자는 집에 오자마자 다른 누구보다 먼저 로티를 찾아가 그녀가 마음에 바라던 모든 것이라고 말한다. 또 밤늦게까지 그녀 곁에 머물며 지난날과 미래를 이야기했다고 서술한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. 의심, 짜증, 죄책감을 보여 주는 표현은 지문에 없으므로 B, C, D는 틀리다.

items.passage:
I "saw" all right, and accepted the proposition, but the odds seemed against us, because the town was one of the most unfriendly along the line. We picked out a house near the track. As a rule such houses have been "begged out," but we reasoned that if our story would go at all it would go there, and besides the house was convenient for catching the next freight-train.

As we approached the back door I was careful to talk to Red on my fingers, thinking that somebody might be watching us. A motherly old lady answered our knock. I told her Red's story in my best manner, filling it out with convincing details.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To explain why the narrator decided to stop traveling by freight train
To describe how the narrator and Red carefully set up a ruse to get help
To show that the town's residents were kinder than the narrator expected
To portray the narrator's friendship with a motherly old woman
items.explanation: 화자와 레드는 비우호적인 마을에서도 이야기가 통할 집을 골랐고 다음 화물열차를 타기 편한 위치까지 계산했다. 또 누가 볼까 봐 손가락으로 대화하며 레드의 사연을 그럴듯한 세부로 꾸며 말한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 여행 중단, C의 마을 평가, D의 우정은 지문의 초점이 아니다.

items.passage: We had sunk together into the slough of despond, and she contrived to scramble out of it and leave me in the mire. She was clever enough to make use of me to accomplish her escape, sent me out among hard-hearted humanity to borrow, beg, or steal the means by which she meant to separate herself from my fallen fortunes. Do you think I came across the world to seek for her? No, Dick, I am not such a fool. I have been cheated once. I shall never be her dupe again. Do you think I could ever trust her any more?--that if fortune smiled upon us, and she pretended to love me, I could feel any confidence in her truth, any security in her affection?
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The speaker hopes to find the woman and win back her love.
The speaker blames himself alone for their shared misfortune.
The speaker insists he will never again trust a woman who deceived him.
The speaker asks Dick to help him borrow money for a journey.
items.explanation: 화자는 그녀가 자신을 이용해 빠져나갔고 자신은 진창에 남겨졌다고 말한다. 이어 그녀를 찾으러 온 것이 아니며 다시는 속지 않겠다고 하고, 앞으로 그녀의 진심을 믿을 수 없다고 묻는다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 반대이고, B는 그녀를 탓하는 태도와 어긋나며, D는 과거 사건을 잘못 쓴 것이다.

items.passage:
I did not see it then--I never did see it!

Something he murmured, to the effect that he supposed the bag was what I was looking for. In what language he spoke I know not; it was more that by the action accompanying the mumbled sounds I gathered his meaning, than that I heard anything articulate.

I thanked him, of course, mechanically, so to say, though I began to feel as if he were an evil spirit haunting me. I could only hope that the splendid lock to the bag had defied all curiosity, but I felt in a fever to be alone again, and able to satisfy myself that nothing had been tampered with.

The thought recalled my wandering faculties. How long had I been asleep?
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “recalled my wandering faculties” most nearly suggests that the narrator
options: remembered a language he had once studied
forgot what he had been looking for
regained his focus after being in a dazed state
began to wander away from the stranger
items.explanation: 화자는 낯선 이의 말을 알아듣지 못하고 기계적으로 감사하며 혼란스러운 상태였다. 가방이 무사한지 확인하고 싶다는 생각이 떠오르자 정신이 돌아왔고, 곧 얼마나 잠들어 있었는지 묻는다. 따라서 흩어진 정신을 다시 모았다는 C가 정답이다. A, B, D는 구절의 비유적 의미와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Eight miles meant nearly three hours’ steaming for us, and I could also see suspicious ripples at the upper end of the reach. Nevertheless, I was annoyed beyond expression at the delay, and most unreasonably, too, since one night more could not matter much after so many months. As we had plenty of wood, and caution was the word, I brought up in the middle of the stream. The reach was narrow, straight, with high sides like a railway cutting. The dusk came gliding into it long before the sun had set. The current ran smooth and swift, but a dumb immobility sat on the banks.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a dumb immobility sat on the banks” most nearly suggests that the riverbanks
options: were crowded with people waiting silently
were too steep for the boat to approach
were slowly being worn away by the current
were eerily silent and still
items.explanation: 화자는 해가 지기 전부터 어둠이 좁은 수로에 스며들었다고 묘사한다. 물살은 빠르게 흘렀지만 강둑에는 말없는 정적이 앉아 있었다는 대비로 섬뜩한 고요함을 드러낸다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 사람들, B의 경사, C의 침식은 구절의 의미가 아니다.

items.passage:
"I had grottos, and fountains, and orange-tree groves,
I had all that enchantment has told;
I had sweet shady walks for the gods and their loves,
I had mountains of coral and gold.

"But a storm that I felt not had risen and rolled,
While wrapped in a slumber I lay;
And when I looked out in the morning, behold,
My Castle was carried away.

"It passed over rivers and valleys and groves,
The world it was all in my view;
I thought of my friends, of their fates, of their loves,
And often, full often, of you.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “My Castle was carried away” most nearly suggests that the speaker
options: lost the splendid world of the imagination
fled from a real fortress during a storm
gave away riches to friends
moved to a new home in the mountains
items.explanation: 화자는 동굴, 분수, 산호와 황금의 산 등 마법 같은 것들을 가졌다고 나열한다. 그러나 잠든 사이 일어난 폭풍에 성이 날아갔다고 하며, 그 성은 상상 속 화려한 꿈을 가리킨다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B, C, D는 비유를 문자 그대로 읽거나 근거 없는 해석이다.

items.passage: Quite different will be the impression made upon those--and they are yet too few--who have learned that the method of science is the common-sense method of cautiously weighing evidence and withholding judgment where evidence is not forthcoming. If talking about remote and difficult subjects suffice to make one scientific, then is M. Figuier scientific to a quite terrible degree. He writes about the starry heavens as if he had been present at the hour of creation, or had at least accompanied the Arabian prophet on his famous night-journey. Nor is his knowledge of physiology and other abstruse sciences at all less remarkable.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “as if he had been present at the hour of creation” most nearly suggests that Figuier
options: studies the night sky with great patience
writes with a certainty his evidence does not justify
believes deeply in ancient religious accounts
rarely writes about remote or difficult subjects
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 과학의 방법이 증거를 신중히 따지고 증거가 없으면 판단을 보류하는 것이라고 먼저 정의한다. 그런데 피기에는 하늘에 대해 창조의 순간에 그 자리에 있었던 것처럼 쓴다고 하여 지나친 확신을 비꼰다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A, C, D는 풍자의 의도를 놓친 해석이다.

items.passage:
Looking back now over the field we have traversed, what is the verdict? Are we going backward or forward? To be standing still would be to lose ground. Nothing stands still in this community of ours, with its ever-swelling population, least of all the problem of the children of the poor. It got the start of our old indifference once, and we have had a long and wearisome race of it, running it down.

But we have run it down. We are moving forward, and indifference will not again trap us into defeat. Evidence is multiplying on every hand to show that interest in the children is increasing. The personal service, that counts for so infinitely much more than money, is more freely given day by day, and no longer as a fashionable fad, but as a duty too long neglected.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a long and wearisome race” most nearly suggests
options: a sporting contest held for poor children
a quick victory that surprised the community
a prolonged, tiring struggle to catch up with a problem
a dispute among citizens over population growth
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 빈곤 아동 문제가 과거 무관심을 앞질렀다고 말하며 그것을 뒤쫓는 경주에 비유한다. 이어 우리는 마침내 그것을 따라잡았고 앞으로 나아가고 있다고 하여 긴 노력의 결과를 강조한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 문자 그대로의 해석이고, B는 길고 지친다는 표현과 반대이며, D는 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Entering the kitchen with her light step, she brought the morning sunshine with her. The old people had already engaged in differences of opinion, but they commonly ______ open warfare in her presence. There were the usual last things to be done for breakfast, offices that belonged to her as her grandmother's assistant. She took yesterday's soda biscuits out of the steamer where they were warming and softening; brought an apple pie and a plate of seed cakes from the pantry; settled the coffee with a piece of dried fish skin and an egg shell; and transferred some fried potatoes from the spider to a covered dish.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: escalated
announced
resumed
suspended
items.explanation: 노인들은 이미 의견 다툼을 시작했지만 그녀가 아침 햇살을 가져온다고 묘사된다. 그러므로 그녀 앞에서는 공공연한 다툼을 잠시 멈춘다는 의미의 단어가 들어가야 하므로 D가 정답이다. A와 C는 다툼이 더 심해지거나 다시 시작된다는 뜻이라 맥락과 반대이고, B는 의미가 통하지 않는다.

items.passage:
I told my story; for I felt that if the senator could trust me, I could ______ him. I did not say anything about my half-formed intention to run away. The squire was very sorry there was any trouble; but, as it was a family matter, he did not like to say much about it, though he promised to do all he could for me.

"I think I won't go any farther, Buck," said he. "I suppose you will despise me, for you know me better than any other person."
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: trust
doubt
avoid
flatter
items.explanation: 화자는 상원의원이 자신을 믿을 수 있다면 자신도 그를 믿을 수 있다고 느껴 이야기를 털어놓았다. 앞 절의 trust me와 짝을 이루어 상호 신뢰를 나타내야 하므로 A가 정답이다. B와 C는 이야기를 털어놓는 행동과 모순되고, D는 문맥상 근거가 없다.

items.passage: For instance, an American gentleman described to me how it fared with him on attempting to land a few years since. He and a friend made a bargain with a respectable man to put them ashore. He called a boatman, into whose boat they got with their luggage. No sooner had the man rowed a little way from the ship than he stopped and ______ the instant payment of a sum four times the amount that had been agreed upon. The travellers said they had made an agreement with his master, and he was bound to carry it out. He replied that he had no master; that the boat was his, that the oars were his, and that he would neither take them back to the ship nor row them ashore unless they complied with his request.

items.explanation: 뱃사공은 약속된 금액의 네 배를 요구했고, 여행자들이 거부하면 배를 움직이지 않겠다고 위협했다. 따라서 즉시 지불을 강하게 요구했다는 B가 정답이다. A와 C는 돈을 받으려는 뱃사공의 행동과 반대이고, D는 즉시라는 말과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
The bees see them from a distance; they are ______ by the bright colors and fly to visit the touch-me-nots. They search for honey, and of course they find it, for the touch-me-not has wisely provided nectar for bees and birds.

The pretty yellow flowers contain rich honey in the little spur at the back. The end of the spur turns down, and it is in this turned-down tip the honey is made. From there it runs into the upper part of the spur, where the bees can reach it.

The moist roadside in many places is dotted with yellow touch-me-not flowers. They hang like earrings from their stems, and many call the plant “jewelweed” because of them. It is a pretty sight in the morning to see the bright jewels sparkling in the dew.
